question: Should OpenClaw core support cross-gateway session messaging directly, or should this remain a plugin/bridge capability until a broader federation contract is approved?
rationale: The requested behavior is missing, but the implementation shape affects gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, and core-vs-plugin responsibility.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define gateway-to-gateway identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics before landing a core implementation.

options.title: Plugin Or MCP Bridge First
options.body: Keep core gateway-local and expose only missing plugin/API seams needed for external bridges to implement cross-gateway routing safely.

options.title: Wait For Broader FRD
options.body: Hold this concrete feature behind the broader federation design issue until maintainers settle transport and tenant-scoped operator policy.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define gateway-to-gateway identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics before landing a core implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the session-tool, gateway config, and gatewayUrl security boundary points to this owner candidate.
